decisive_moments.reason: Pro usefully narrowed the conjecture to cumulative scientific understanding and distinguished individual use of black-box prediction from system-level value.
Con identified the central burden problem: showing that explanation is generally more valuable, rather than merely sometimes useful, and emphasized replication and public checkability.

Pro clarified a defensible conditional thesis—explanation is more valuable when it makes verification portable, supports intervention, or enables transfer—but this qualification weakened the original broad conjecture.
Con correctly maintained that conditional benefits do not establish general superiority and tied explanatory credit to identifiable mechanisms, accessible evidence, and discriminating replication.

flags.quote: I claim greater value when explanation earns its keep by enabling transfer, intervention, or discriminating tests.
Explanations deserve extra credit when they earn it through successful, discriminating predictions—not because causal understanding has a default premium.
